_: WHICH ASSET ANSWERS WHICH SURFACE. Committing this file is what starts a
fetch — the workflow triggers on it and on nothing else, so the download
happens when somebody decides it should and never as a side effect of a
code change.
CHOSEN FROM catalogue.json, LOCALLY, IN SECONDS. That file holds all 2,005
materials and which sizes each publishes, pulled once, so none of these
picks cost a run to make. It also settled the question that stopped the
first attempt: the per-term search returned ZERO for `PavingStones` and
`RoofingTiles`, and the catalogue shows 162 and 31 respectively. The search
endpoint was the unreliable instrument, not the library — which is the
third time this month that suspecting the instrument first was correct.
PICKED BY NAME, WHICH IS AN HONEST LIMITATION. No image can be seen from
this container, so these are chosen on category and on being early, stable
ids rather than on how they look. `pack_check.py` verifies FORM — square,
power-of-two, non-empty, present under the name the game looks up — and has
no opinion about beauty. The visual pass happens after they land, by
looking at them, which is the only way that has ever worked here.
THE PALETTE DOES THE WORK ANYWAY. `SurfaceSpec` tints every surface toward
the noir blue-grey and darkens it, verified 9/9 on 2026-07-28, so an albedo
that arrives slightly wrong in hue is corrected by the material rather than
by re-picking. What cannot be corrected is a texture of the wrong THING,
which is what the category choice below is for.

RE-TRIGGERED 2026-07-31 (a). The first commit of this file ran the INVENTORY and SKIPPED the fetch — the workflow routed on `github.event.commits.*.added`, which is an array of arrays that `join()` does not flatten, so both branches of the condition read false and the negated one won. The run reported success while doing nothing. Routing is now a `paths:` filter in two separate workflow files, which GitHub evaluates itself, so there is no condition left to be wrong.

RE-TRIGGERED 2026-07-31 (c). All twelve downloaded — and `pack_check` refused two of them for not being square: kerb (Concrete034) and brick_red (Bricks075A) are both 1024x512. The instinct was right and the rule was wrong. A non-square texture tiles perfectly well; what broke is that `AssetLibrary` applied ONE tiling factor to both axes, so a 2:1 image got twice the texel density across as up. That is fixed in `Core/TextureFit`, which splits the correction across the axes so texels come out square and the surface still reads at its authored size, held there by fourteen CoreTests. These two ids stay: replacing them would mean guessing at dimensions the catalogue does not record, and the renderer has stopped making the assumption that made them a problem.

RE-TRIGGERED 2026-07-31 (b). The routing fix worked and the fetch ran, and all twelve surfaces failed in six seconds with a bare `StopIteration`. The fetch resolved each id through `?q=<assetId>` and took the result whose assetId matched; nothing matched, for any of the twelve. THE SEARCH ENDPOINT AGAIN — the same one that reported zero PavingStones against 162 in the catalogue and zero RoofingTiles against 31. Three times is not a coincidence, so the fetch path no longer asks it anything: links come from the committed catalogue where present, and otherwise from the paginated list endpoint that produced all 2,005 materials in the first place. The catalogue now records each asset's download link too, so the next fetch is twelve downloads and no lookup at all.

RE-TRIGGERED 2026-08-16: 1K to 2K, and roughness joins colour+normal. Jafar's standing order is best-possible with available resources; the target machine is an M5, the camera walks up to walls, and 2K is where brick stops smearing at arm's length. All twelve ids publish 2K-JPG (checked against the committed catalogue before this commit, zero runs spent). The committed catalogue links are 1K zips, so the fetcher now refuses a catalogue link whose filename lacks the wanted size and resolves those through the list endpoint instead — otherwise this commit would have downloaded 1K and labelled it 2K.

RE-TRIGGERED 2026-08-18: VARIETY, the ladder rung after scale. Twelve surfaces meant every brick building in the city wore the SAME PHOTOGRAPH, and at 376 buildings that repetition is what a street reads as now that there are enough of them to compare. One extra variant each for the five surfaces that fill a street view — the two bricks, plaster, roof, concrete — picked per building by the position hash that already picks the surface. Five new ids rather than fifty: the catalogue offers 113 bricks and 154 paving stones, so the limit is repository weight and not availability, and doubling the facade set is the cheapest visible half of that. Picked by category and stable id, unseen, exactly as the first twelve were; the visual pass happens when they land, by looking.
